hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: LightGBM with a lambdarank objective, groups capped at 6 consecutive rows per user to match the evaluation list shape, over base5 plus out-of-fold item aggregates, will beat the pointwise FM baseline by a large margin.
rationale: Two structural defects of the baseline are fixed at once: the loss now optimises within-list order rather than calibrated per-impression probability, and the training groups are shaped like the ~6-item lists actually scored, so the NDCG position discount lambdarank applies matches the discount the metric applies. Trees also consume a continuous item-quality prior (video/author long-view rate, impression count) that varies across the rows of a single user's list and can therefore reorder it, which is exactly the kind of signal an embedding-only FM has to rediscover from a 1.14M-row id interaction.
expected_gain_derivation: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] says the loss/metric mismatch is unaddressed and [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] ranks loss change first, so the objective switch alone should be the biggest single move; [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] says untuned grouping trains on 43-row lists while scoring 6-row lists, so chunk=6 removes a second mismatch. GBDT+pairwise over the same fields typically lands 0.63-0.65 on this kind of within-user task versus 0.6014, i.e. +0.03 to +0.05; [WITHIN_USER_RANKING] plus [HIGH_COVERAGE] (99.9% of valid videos seen in train, so item rates are populated) adds maybe +0.01-0.02 from item_agg. I discount ~15% for the chance item_agg trips the drift check, giving +0.050.

block_justifications.base5: The five baseline fields are the reference feature set and video_id/author_id/dur_bucket vary across a user's rows, so they are the only base fields that can reorder a list [WITHIN_USER_RANKING].
block_justifications.item_agg: Out-of-fold video/author long-view and click rates are item-level and therefore differ between the rows of one user's list, giving a directly reorderable quality prior that the FM must otherwise infer from sparse ids [HIGH_COVERAGE].

hypothesis: Adding duration features (log duration plus within-user duration percentile rank) to the LightGBM lambdarank/chunk-6 setup will lift primary well above the FM baseline.
rationale: long_view is a duration-thresholded outcome: short videos are far more likely to be long-viewed, and the base5 field dur_bucket only encodes a coarse absolute bucket. The percentile rank of a candidate's duration WITHIN the user's own list is a purely relative quantity, which is exactly the kind of signal that can reorder a ~6-item list, and it is unavailable to any absolute-bucket encoding. This is the organizers' listed but untried duration-bias lever.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] names duration-bias modelling as untouched, and [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]/[SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] mean a within-list relative rank feature acts directly on the scored quantity. The organizers' dead ends were all user-constant or capacity moves; a row-varying, list-relative feature is structurally different. Iteration 1 showed the lambdarank+item_agg frame sits at 0.6011, so I predict duration features move it to ~0.616, i.e. +0.015 vs the 0.6014 baseline, an order of magnitude above the 0.0008 seed noise [SEED_NOISE].

hypothesis: A listwise rank_xendcg LightGBM trained on 4-row chronological chunks (matching the valid median list length) with an explicit user-personalisation block (cross_agg) plus categorical regularisation will finally break past 0.6014, because it supplies the user x item interaction the trees cannot learn from raw ids.
rationale: The organizers state the user_id x video_id interaction absorbs most of the learnable signal; an FM represents that with embeddings, but LightGBM cannot construct it from two high-cardinality categoricals in 1.14M rows, which is exactly why my two tree runs landed on top of the FM number instead of above it. cross_agg hands the tree that interaction pre-computed and out-of-fold (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, duration relative to the user's own long-viewed duration) as continuous columns that vary across a user's rows, so they can actually reorder a list. Simultaneously I switch the structural axis: rank_xendcg is a listwise softmax with no position discount, which matches nDCG@5 over a ~6-item list where essentially the whole list must be ordered, and chunk=4 makes training lists the same shape as the valid median rather than 43-row lists. Categorical smoothing is raised and max_cat_threshold lowered to stop the id fields from soaking up splits they cannot generalise from.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD] and [ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD] say static fields and capacity are exhausted, and my iterations 1-2 show item-level and duration-level signal is also exhausted (0.6011, 0.6011, both within [SEED_NOISE] of the 0.6014 baseline). By elimination the only unspent signal is the user x item interaction the organizers name as dominant plus the behaviour-derived affinity they list as unexplored [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED]. The FM gets 0.6014 with that interaction learned implicitly and no item quality prior; a tree with the interaction supplied explicitly AND item aggregates AND duration should exceed it by more than seed noise. Gap to [CEILING] is 0.247, so a 5% recovery of it is 0.012; I take that as the point estimate, with real downside risk to 0.000 if cross_agg is dominated by user-constant components [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT].
